The Honda CR-V family

7 generations and variants in the Index, 1997–present. Oldest first; every card opens the full page, with its own versions, figures and story.

  1. 1997–2001

    Honda CR-V (first generation)

    The first CR-V, 1997–2001: a tall, Civic-based wagon with optional all-wheel drive and a picnic table in the cargo floor, and the best seller in its class until 2001.

    126 hp10.9 sec 0-60524,661 built
  2. 2002–2006

    Honda CR-V (second generation)

    The second-generation CR-V, 2002–2006: a full redesign on Civic bones with a 160-hp 2.4-liter, and Car and Driver's Best Small SUV for 2002 and 2003.

    160 hp8.4 sec 0-60759,703 built
  3. 2007–2011

    Honda CR-V (third generation)

    The third-generation CR-V, 2007–2011: lower and wider, with a liftgate instead of a swing-out door, and America's best-selling SUV in 2007 and 2008.

    166 hp9.1 sec 0-601,029,740 built
  4. 2012–2016

    Honda CR-V (fourth generation)

    The fourth-generation CR-V, 2012–2016: 185 hp and smarter all-wheel drive at launch, then a 2015 update with direct injection, a CVT and driver-assist safety features.

    185 hp8.5 sec 0-601,623,557 built
    2.4-liter, 2012–2014 · 2.4-liter, 2015–2016
  5. 2017–2022

    Honda CR-V (fifth generation)

    The fifth-generation CR-V, 2017–2022: roomy and easy to live with, with a 1.5-liter turbo in most versions, 75.8 cubic feet of cargo space and, from 2020, the first US CR-V Hybrid.

    190 hp7.6 sec 0-602,064,004 built
    1.5-liter turbo · 2.4-liter · Hybrid
  6. 2023–present

    Honda CR-V (sixth generation)

    The sixth-generation CR-V, from 2023: bigger and calmer, with a 190-hp turbo or a 204-hp hybrid now offered with front-wheel drive and rated at up to 40 mpg.

    204 hp7.9 sec 0-601,539,675 built
    Hybrid · 1.5-liter turbo
  7. 2025–present

    Honda CR-V e:FCEV

    America's first production plug-in hydrogen fuel cell vehicle: a CR-V with 29 miles of battery range and 270 miles in all, leased only in California.

    174 hp8.5 sec 0-60
